verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah (the same was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon),
which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah, and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah, even to this day, these twenty-three years, Yahweh’s word has come to me, and I have spoken to you, rising up early and speaking; but you have not listened.
Yahweh has sent to you all his servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them (but you have not listened, nor inclined your ear to hear)
saying, “Return now everyone from his evil way, and from the evil of your doings, and dwell in the land that Yahweh has given to you and to your fathers, from of old and even forever more.
Don’t go after other gods to serve them or worship them, and don’t provoke me to anger with the work of your hands; and I will do you no harm.”
“Yet you have not listened to me,” says Yahweh; “that you may provoke me to anger with the work of your hands to your own hurt.”
Therefore Yahweh of Armies says: “Because you have not heard my words,

behold, I will send and take all the families of the north,” says Yahweh, “and I will send to Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will bring them against this land, and against its inhabitants, and against all these nations around. I will utterly destroy them, and make them an astonishment, and a hissing, and perpetual desolations.
Moreover I will take from them the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.
This whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

“It shall happen, when seventy years are accomplished, that I will punish the king of Babylon, and that nation,” says Yahweh, “for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans; and I will make it desolate forever.
I will bring on that land all my words which I have pronounced against it, even all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations.
For many nations and great kings shall make bondservants of them, even of them; and I will recompense them according to their deeds, and according to the work of their hands.”
For Yahweh, the God of Israel, says to me: “take this cup of the wine of wrath at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send you, to drink it.
They shall drink, and reel back and forth, and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them.”
Then took I the cup at Yahweh’s hand, and made all the nations to drink, to whom Yahweh had sent me:
Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, and its kings, and its princes, to make them a desolation, an astonishment, a hissing, and a curse, as it is today;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, and his servants, and his princes, and all his people;
and all the mixed people, and all the kings of the land of the Uz, and all the kings of the Philistines, and Ashkelon, and Gaza, and Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom, and Moab, and the children of Ammon;
and all the kings of Tyre, and all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the isle which is beyond the sea;
Dedan, and Tema, and Buz, and all who have the corners of their beard cut off;
and all the kings of Arabia, and all the kings of the mixed people who dwell in the wilderness;
and all the kings of Zimri, and all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of the Medes;
and all the kings of the north, far and near, one with another; and all the kingdoms of the world, which are on the surface of the earth: and the king of Sheshach shall drink after them.
“You shall tell them, ‘Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says: “Drink, and be drunk, vomit, fall, and rise no more, because of the sword which I will send among you.”’
It shall be, if they refuse to take the cup at your hand to drink, then you shall tell them, ‘Yahweh of Armies says: “You shall surely drink.

For, behold, I begin to work evil at the city which is called by my name; and should you be utterly unpunished? You shall not be unpunished; for I will call for a sword on all the inhabitants of the earth, says Yahweh of Armies.”’

“Therefore prophesy you against them all these words, and tell them, “‘Yahweh will roar from on high, and utter his voice from his holy habitation; he will mightily roar against his fold. He will give a shout, as those who tread grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth.

A noise shall come even to the end of the earth; for Yahweh has a controversy with the nations; he will enter into judgment with all flesh: as for the wicked, he will give them to the sword,”’ says Yahweh.”
Yahweh of Armies says, “Behold, evil shall go out from nation to nation, and a great storm shall be raised up from the uttermost parts of the earth.”

The slain of Yahweh shall be at that day from one end of the earth even to the other end of the earth: they shall not be lamented, neither gathered, nor buried; they shall be dung on the surface of the ground.
Wail, you shepherds, and cry; and wallow in dust, you leader of the flock; for the days of your slaughter and of your dispersions are fully come, and you shall fall like a goodly vessel.
The shepherds shall have no way to flee, nor the leader of the flock to escape.
A voice of the cry of the shepherds, and the wailing of the leader of the flock, for Yahweh lays waste their pasture.
The peaceable folds are brought to silence because of the fierce anger of Yahweh.
He has left his covert, as the lion; for their land has become an astonishment because of the fierceness of the oppression, and because of his fierce anger.

footnotes.content: The timing here is precise—Jehoiakim's fourth year, Nebuchadnezzar's first. History and prophecy meet at a fixed point. Even in exile's shadow, Yahweh's word keeps its clock.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah speaks to all—priests, merchants, warriors, mothers. The Lord will not let His word land in silence, though hearts resist. Everyone hears.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twenty-three years of rising early, speaking faithfully, never listened to. The prophet's loneliness runs deep—but notice: he kept rising. Faithfulness in exile from the heart is its own reward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not one prophet, but many—all rising early, all sent, all refused. The Lord is not stingy with His messengers. He keeps speaking even to those who clap their ears shut.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The invitation stands simple: turn from evil, stay in the land, dwell as the Lord's own. The path home is always open before judgment comes. This is mercy, offered plainly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Two commands, both rooted in love: stop chasing other gods, stop provoking the One who loves you. He says, 'I will do you no harm'—if you turn. The offer is real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem's refusal to listen shows a tragic pattern: they provoke Yahweh to anger by their own hands, then feel the sting they forged. Sin's wages are often paid in coin we mint ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh of Armies—the Lord who commands heaven and earth—speaks now with terrible authority. When refusal hardens into habit, what was mercy must become justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nebuchadnezzar is called 'my servant'—not because he worships the Lord, but because Yahweh uses him. Even a pagan king is an instrument in the hands of the Almighty. Nothing escapes His purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No laughter, no wedding songs, no grain grinding, no lamplight. The sounds of home and hope go silent. Judgment strips a land bare—but notice it does not strip away God's sovereignty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seventy years—a long time to live under foreign rule. But the number itself is a mercy: it ends. Exiles know then that the Lord has not forgotten, has counted the days.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After Judah's punishment comes Babylon's. The Lord is not cruel to one nation and indulgent to another. He judges all iniquity. The arc of His justice bends, but it does bend toward righteousness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the words Jeremiah has spoken are now being written down—recorded in history, certified in the Book. What seemed like lonely, unheeded words are actually forever words.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even enslavers will be enslaved. The Lord does not turn a blind eye to those who make bondservants of others. Justice circles round—nations reap what they have sown.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cup of wrath—a metaphor Jeremiah himself must drink first, then hold out to others. In Scripture, to drink the cup means to take judgment fully, to taste its bitterness. The prophet shares the burden.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nations drink and reel, stumbling as if drunk with judgment. The sword follows the cup—wrath is not empty threat but actual consequence. Yet even here, the Lord acts with purpose, not chaos.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah obeys. He takes the cup and makes all the nations drink—a terrible responsibility, faithfully carried. He does not flinch from the hard word Yahweh has given him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem first—Judah's own kings and princes. There is no favoritism in judgment. The Lord's own people are not exempt from consequence. Love that does not discipline is not love at all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pharaoh and his court—Egypt's great power bows to the same cup. No throne is too high for Yahweh's judgment to reach.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Philistine cities—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, Ashdod—each with its own history, each now summoned to drink. The Lord does not forget old enemies or spare them from His reckoning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Edom, Moab, Ammon—related peoples to the east, now their turn. Kinship offers no immunity. The Lord's justice does not run on tribal logic.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tyre and Sidon, great merchant cities of the sea—their trade routes, their wealth, cannot buy them free from judgment. The Lord's reach extends to every corner of the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dedan, Tema, Buz—distant places, names that sound foreign to Jerusalem ears. Yet the Lord has His eye on them too. No nation, however remote, escapes His attention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The kings of Arabia, wandering peoples of the wilderness—all summoned. The settled and the nomadic, the mighty and the overlooked, all drink from the same cup.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zimri, Elam, Media—the great powers of the east also bend to Yahweh's will. Distance and might are no shield against the Lord's judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All kingdoms, far and near, east and west—the earth itself is Yahweh's domain, and His justice encompasses it all. 'Sheshach' (Babylon) drinks last, as if the greatest power faces judgment last.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command is stark: Drink, be drunk, vomit, fall, rise no more. The language is brutally honest about collapse. Judgment is not refined; it is total ruin, unless grace intervenes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Refusal is not an option. If they would not drink willing, they shall drink by force. Judgment is not a negotiation. Once Yahweh has spoken, the word will not return empty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem first, then all the earth. The Lord begins His work of judgment at His own house—that is mercy hidden in severity. If the holy city itself does not escape, no refuge exists.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh roars from on high as a lion roars, as men roar treading grapes. His voice shakes from His holy habitation—no one can mistake what is coming. The thunder of judgment is the sound of His presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The noise reaches the end of the earth—Yahweh's controversy with the nations is universal. He enters judgment with all flesh. The wicked receive the sword. All things are open before Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Evil goes forth nation to nation, a great storm rising from the earth's edge. This is no localized trouble—judgment rolls across the world like a tempest no power can stop.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The slain of Yahweh lie unlamented, unburied—a terrible image of a land so broken that even the rites of the dead are forgotten. Yet even this speaks to the totality of Yahweh's work—nothing escapes His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The shepherds are told to wail—those who led Israel now must weep. Their slaughter and scattering are fully determined. The beautiful vessel, Israel, will be broken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There is no way to flee, no way to escape. The shepherds have nowhere to run. When judgment comes with the Lord's authority, refuge becomes impossible.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cry and wailing of leaders echoes—the pastures are laid waste. What once fed the flock now cannot sustain. Even the land itself becomes an accuser.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The peaceful folds brought to silence—no more bleating, no more gentle grazing. The fierce anger of Yahweh is visible in the sudden hush, the absence of all that was familiar.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo here: when Yahweh rises as a lion to execute judgment, He is not distant from us either. The fierceness of His opposition to evil remains, though now it comes through Christ's intercession and our own repentance. We have a way out they missed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
